main.title: Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands
main.subtitle: The Plan Begins Before the Fight
main.summary: A four-person squad works across a fictionalized Bolivia in Ghost Recon Wildlands. Reconnaissance, coordinated shots and open approaches let players plan together, then adapt when a careful operation becomes chaotic.

cards.heading: Four Soldiers, Many Approaches
cards.text: Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands places a four-person squad in an open reconstruction of Bolivia. Reconnaissance, synchronized shots and approaches from different directions give cooperative players room to plan a fight before they begin it.

cards.heading: Reconnaissance Before Combat
cards.text: Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands is a tactical cover based shooter game set in an open world environment and played from a third-person perspective with an optional first-person view for gun aiming. Players control members of the Delta Company, First Battalion, 5th Special Forces Group, also known as "Ghosts", an elite special operations unit of the United States Army under the Joint Special Operations Command. It does not feature the futuristic setting used in Advanced Warfighter and Future Soldier, and instead adopts a modern-day setting, similar to the original Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon. As a result, the equipment featured in the game is based on contemporary weapons and gear commonly used by military forces around the world. It features some original equipment, such as flying drones that can be used to tag enemies and show objectives. These drones have limited use beyond reconnaissance until upgraded, unlocking several abilities that can be used for tactical benefit.

cards.heading: Terrain Changes the Plan
cards.text: The game is the first entry in the series to feature an open world environment. Set in contemporary Bolivia, the map consists of nine different types of terrain, such as mountains, jungles, forests, deserts, salt flats, and more. It also introduces a dynamic weather system as well as a day-night cycle. Completing missions during daytime allows players to spot enemies more easily, while completing missions at night offers better concealment and easier infiltration due to some guardsmen being asleep. Players are tasked with making observations and planning out their course of action before carrying out missions. A variety of vehicles, such as dirt bikes, helicopters and dune buggies, are featured in the game. Unlike its predecessors, Wildlands features several side-missions.

cards.heading: A Squad of Players or AI Companions
cards.text: It features cooperative multiplayer mode, in which players can be joined by up to three other players to explore the game's world and to complete campaign missions. The game can be played solo, in which the player will be accompanied by three AI teammates, which the player can give orders to, if a player wants a more "lone wolf" playstyle they can be disabled via the settings. A competitive multiplayer mode has been released as part of a free update on October 10, 2017. It features an elimination type of game mode in a timed 4v4 match with revives. Players can level up through multiplayer gameplay which enables them to improve the different class of characters available.

main.title: Thimbleweed Park
main.subtitle: A Body Is Only the Beginning
main.summary: Thimbleweed Park turns a small-town mystery into a shared investigation across five playable characters.

cards.heading: A Town With Too Many Secrets
cards.text: Ron Gilbert announced Thimbleweed Park's release on 30 March 2017. The mystery is set in 1987, in a town with an abandoned circus, a strange hotel and a burnt-out pillow factory. A body under a bridge brings investigators into a place whose other problems quickly demand attention.

cards.heading: Five Lives in the Same Mystery
cards.text: Five playable characters bring different concerns into the same story. Agents Ray and Reyes investigate, while aspiring developer Delores, the clown Ransome and the ghost Franklin have their own situations to resolve. Switching between them lets the player see connections that no single character initially understands.

cards.heading: 2017 Meets 1987
cards.text: Ron Gilbert and Gary Winnick returned to the point-and-click adventure form associated with their earlier work. Casual and Hard modes offer different puzzle challenges within the same mystery. Its fictional 1987 town combines an abandoned circus, a strange hotel and a burnt-out factory.

cards.heading: Verbs Shape the Investigation
cards.text: Thimbleweed Park operates on the same principles of early graphic adventure games. Players navigate various scenes from a third person perspective, using various "verb commands" to perform actions, such as "use", "pick up", and "talk to". Verb commands can be used to perform actions such as allowing a character to pick up an object into their inventory, to converse with another character, or to use an object on another item. The game's story is played out across a series of chapters, in which players must complete a specific set of goals to advance to the next chapter, solving a series of puzzles, some of which require the use of more than one character. The game features five different player characters, with the ability to switch between them in the middle of gameplay, similarly to Maniac Mansion.

main.title: Yooka-Laylee
main.subtitle: A new duo from Rare veterans
main.summary: Yooka-Laylee is Playtonic?s 2017 3D platformer, following a chameleon and a bat through worlds expanded with collectible Pagies.

cards.heading: Yooka and Laylee explore together
cards.text: Yooka-Laylee is a 3D platformer released on April 11, 2017. Playtonic brought together developers who had worked at Rare to create a new pair of heroes: Yooka the chameleon and Laylee the bat. They explore large worlds, learn abilities and collect Pagies to open or expand areas.

cards.heading: A crowdfunded successor to Banjo-Kazooie
cards.text: The project?s Kickstarter campaign raised more than two million pounds. Backers supported a game presented as a successor to Banjo-Kazooie, made by veterans of that style of platforming. Crowdfunding gave Playtonic the resources to develop its first game.

cards.heading: Pagies open and expand worlds
cards.text: Pagies can unlock new worlds or expand those already visited. An expanded area adds routes, characters and challenges, leaving the player to choose between exploring elsewhere or returning to familiar ground. Collected objects therefore determine which places become available.

cards.heading: A familiar style divides reviewers
cards.text: Reviews welcomed the return of this kind of 3D platformer but criticised camera behaviour, the quantity of collectibles and the size of some worlds. The response showed how closely Playtonic?s revival followed the strengths and frustrations of its predecessors.

main.title: Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia
main.subtitle: Intelligent Systems · Nintendo 3DS
main.summary: Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia is Intelligent Systems' Nintendo 3DS reconstruction of Fire Emblem Gaiden. Alm joins an army resisting the invasion of Zofia, while Celica travels in search of the missing goddess Mila. Their separate routes cross a continent whose political troubles are entangled with the powers its people worship. The player manages both groups, moving between tactical battles, settlements and dungeons. Familiar characters return with new writing, voices and illustrations, giving the earlier adventure a substantially expanded dramatic presentation.

cards.heading: Two journeys across Valentia
cards.text: Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia is Intelligent Systems' Nintendo 3DS reconstruction of Fire Emblem Gaiden. Alm joins an army resisting the invasion of Zofia, while Celica travels in search of the missing goddess Mila. Their separate routes cross a continent whose political troubles are entangled with the powers its people worship. The player manages both groups, moving between tactical battles, settlements and dungeons. Familiar characters return with new writing, voices and illustrations, giving the earlier adventure a substantially expanded dramatic presentation.

cards.heading: Leave the battlefield and enter a dungeon
cards.text: The world map connects battles and other destinations, but entering a dungeon puts a character directly under the player's control. Corridors can be searched for items, and contact with an enemy begins a tactical encounter. Those expeditions introduce fatigue, making supplies and the condition of the group matter across several fights. Back on the grid, spells spend the caster's health and weapons can teach Combat Arts. An ability that wins the current exchange may therefore reduce what its user can safely risk next.

cards.heading: A chance to reconsider a move
cards.text: Mila's Turnwheel allows a limited number of actions to be rewound. A badly judged advance can be examined and changed without repeating the entire battle, making it easier to understand exactly where a plan failed. The feature sits alongside the choice between permanent losses and returning allies. Dungeons, distinct armies and equipment retain Gaiden's unusual place within Fire Emblem, while the Turnwheel supplies a new way to learn its dangers. Alm and Celica remain separate leaders whose parties must each find a workable route forward.

main.title: What Remains of Edith Finch
main.subtitle: A house full of unfinished stories
main.summary: What Remains of Edith Finch is a first-person walking simulator developed by Giant Sparrow and published by Annapurna Interactive.

cards.heading: A first-person story reaches new platforms
cards.text: What Remains of Edith Finch is a first-person walking simulator developed by Giant Sparrow and published by Annapurna Interactive. The game was released in 2017 for PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One; for Nintendo Switch in 2019; for iOS in 2021; and for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S in 2022.

cards.heading: A house of stories and uncertain memories
cards.text: The story follows the seventeen-year-old Edith Finch, the last surviving member of her family, as she returns to her ancestral home for the first time in seven years. Reexploring the house, she uncovers her family's mysterious past and learns about the series of deaths that eventually caused the complete collapse of her family structure. The game is presented as an interconnected anthology. The story utilizes unique media from multiple perspectives and is told through a series of vignettes; however, the player is made to doubt the authenticity of each story being told. The magical realist story touches on themes of free will, fate, memory, and death.

cards.heading: Recognition for storytelling
cards.text: What Remains of Edith Finch received critical acclaim, receiving praise for its immersive storytelling, characters, and presentation; and is considered an example of video games as an art form. Among other awards and nominations, it won Best Game at the 2018 British Academy Games Awards and the Best Narrative category at both The Game Awards 2017 and the 2018 Game Developers Choice Awards.

main.title: Little Nightmares
main.subtitle: Six finds a way through the Maw
main.summary: Little Nightmares follows Six, a child in a yellow raincoat, through the enormous rooms and hostile inhabitants of the Maw.

cards.heading: A child inside the Maw
cards.text: Little Nightmares is Tarsier Studios? 2017 horror adventure, released on April 28. Six, a child in a yellow raincoat, makes her way through the Maw, a vast structure inhabited by distorted adults. Its rooms mix platforming, physics puzzles and stealth.

cards.heading: Ordinary objects become obstacles
cards.text: Six?s size turns familiar objects into obstacles. She climbs shelves, hides beneath tables and looks for handles she can reach. Kitchens and corridors become dangerous when their adult occupants tower over her. A side-on camera shows the depth of these oversized rooms.

cards.heading: Watching, hiding and running
cards.text: Survival depends on watching the inhabitants? routes and choosing when to move. Furniture, shadows and narrow openings offer hiding places, but a poorly timed run can start a chase. Six rarely has a way to fight her pursuers.

cards.heading: The story in the surroundings
cards.text: Very little dialogue explains the Maw. Food, cages, machinery and the behaviour of its inhabitants suggest what happens there. The player pieces together those details while trying to guide Six through it.

main.title: Farpoint
main.subtitle: A weapon held inside an alien world
main.summary: Farpoint is Impulse Gear's virtual-reality science-fiction shooter, released for PlayStation VR on 16 May 2017.

cards.heading: A weapon held inside an alien world
cards.text: Farpoint is Impulse Gear's virtual-reality science-fiction shooter, released for PlayStation VR on 16 May 2017. Stranded on a hostile alien planet, the player searches for the missing team and a route home while confronting its dangerous inhabitants. The adventure combines exploration with firefights in which the weapon occupies the player's own space. Looking across the landscape and raising a gun to respond become connected physical actions, giving the familiar premise of surviving an unknown world a particularly direct relationship with the controller.

cards.heading: Aim through the sights
cards.text: The PS VR Aim Controller tracks the position and orientation of the held weapon. Raising it towards the face lets the player look through its sights, while leaning and ducking change the view around cover. Reaching towards the back switches weapons through a gesture. A DualShock 4 is also supported. Impulse Gear worked with Sony on the peripheral, making the relationship between a physical grip and its virtual counterpart central to the game rather than an accessory added after the shooting was designed.

cards.heading: A survival journey with another player
cards.text: The single-player story is joined by online cooperative challenges, where a second player helps confront enemy groups and cover the surrounding space. The team designed those encounters around the combined effectiveness of two armed players, giving cooperation its own pressure. Later updates added further maps and competitive modes. Stephen Cox composed the score. Farpoint served as an early substantial showcase for the Aim Controller, demonstrating how precise tracking and a familiar two-handed shape could make a console shooter's basic act of aiming feel different in virtual reality.

main.title: ARMS
main.subtitle: Distance, motion and a new cast
main.summary: ARMS is a 2017 Nintendo Switch fighting game in which extendable arms let opponents trade punches, grabs and charged attacks across a 3D arena.

cards.heading: ARMS
cards.text: ARMS is a 2017 fighting game developed and published by Nintendo for Switch. Its fighters use extendable arms to punch, grab, block and dodge across three-dimensional arenas. Up to four players can fight together, controlling their chosen weapons with motion controls or buttons.

cards.heading: Fighting at a distance
cards.text: Arms is a 3D fighting sports game in which up to four players can control one of a variety of fighters, with the player able to perform basic fighting actions using extendable arms such as punching, throwing, blocking and dodging. Each fighter starts with three unique Arms that can be selected in battle, but the use of all other fighters' Arms can be unlocked in the Get Arms mode. All fighters also have unique attributes in combat. When the attack meter is fully charged, players are able to unleash a high-damage "rush attack" against their opponents. Players can also charge their attacks to temporarily increase damage and utilize elemental effects. Each character has a different set of abilities and unique Arms for different strategies.

cards.heading: Two hands, different weapons
cards.text: Players are able to use the system's Joy-Con motion controls or standard button inputs with controllers such as the Pro Controller to operate each Arm individually. Players are also able to customize their Arm load outs, with each Arm being able to be selected independently.

cards.heading: More than a duel
cards.text: Besides the standard fighting mode, Arms features multiple other modes: Versus, Grand Prix, and a variety of Battle modes. In Grand Prix, players take on a set of 10 matches against computer-controlled fighters to win the championship belt. Battle mode consists of volleyball and basketball modes, a target breaking mode, and a survival mode. Players can also play online in a party match lobby with up to 20 players, or in one-on-one ranked matches.

cards.heading: Designing from the arms
cards.text: Character designs started with the arms first with the team working backwards to decide what type of character would possess it, for instance the character of Helix, started with the idea of a fighter whose arms were DNA strands, although the team initially did not know much else about him. Most fighters were designed to fill a gameplay need, although there are some exceptions where a design came first. An early concept for the game had the characters using external devices to punch their opponents; however, this was later dropped in favor of the characters extending their actual arms. Art director Masaaki Ishikawa said that the game's art style was largely influenced by Dragon Ball and Akira. Yabuki has stated that, as opposed to one single protagonist, all of the characters are the protagonists of the game.

main.title: Ever Oasis
main.subtitle: Grezzo · Nintendo 3DS
main.summary: Ever Oasis is Grezzo's Nintendo 3DS action role-playing game about creating a settlement in a world threatened by Chaos. A young Seedling works with the water spirit Esna to establish an oasis and welcome people from the surrounding desert. Exploring distant ruins supplies materials and introduces potential residents. Back home, those discoveries become shops and a larger community. Koichi Ishii, known for his work on Mana, directed an adventure whose two activities support one another: a better settlement helps the next expedition, and the expedition brings something useful home.

cards.heading: Build a refuge in the desert
cards.text: Ever Oasis is Grezzo's Nintendo 3DS action role-playing game about creating a settlement in a world threatened by Chaos. A young Seedling works with the water spirit Esna to establish an oasis and welcome people from the surrounding desert. Exploring distant ruins supplies materials and introduces potential residents. Back home, those discoveries become shops and a larger community. Koichi Ishii, known for his work on Mana, directed an adventure whose two activities support one another: a better settlement helps the next expedition, and the expedition brings something useful home.

cards.heading: A new resident opens another possibility
cards.text: Seedling residents can operate Bloom Booths, shops that need materials gathered outside the oasis. Supplying them produces income and helps the settlement develop. Other residents contribute abilities useful during exploration instead of opening a stall. Welcoming somebody therefore changes more than the population count. A new companion may solve a problem in a dungeon, while another shop can create demand for an item found along the route. The town gradually becomes a practical record of the places visited and the people encountered there.

cards.heading: Take the right companions into the ruins
cards.text: A small party explores the desert and fights directly with weapons, evasive movements and special abilities. The player can switch between companions to use their different tools against enemies or environmental obstacles. Choosing who comes along matters before the group leaves home. Finding materials and completing requests then gives the return journey a purpose beyond reaching safety. Sebastian Schwartz's score accompanies the changing pace between active expeditions and tending the oasis, keeping the refuge at the centre of a world that continually invites another trip outward.

main.title: Splatoon 2
main.subtitle: Ink, territory and cooperation
main.summary: Splatoon 2 is a 2017 third-person shooter game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo Switch. It is the second entry in the Splatoon series as the direct sequel to Splatoon (2015). As with the previous installment, Splatoon 2 consists of online multiplayer game modes alongside a single-player campaign, all featuring combat based around ink-firing weapons.

cards.heading: Splatoon 2
cards.text: Splatoon 2 is a 2017 third-person shooter game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo Switch. It is the second entry in the Splatoon series as the direct sequel to Splatoon (2015). As with the previous installment, Splatoon 2 consists of online multiplayer game modes alongside a single-player campaign, all featuring combat based around ink-firing weapons.

cards.heading: Weapons and ink
cards.text: In online matches, players are equipped with a "main weapon", their primary armament that allows them to spread ink. Each main weapon is assigned a loadout of one "sub weapon" and one "special weapon". Sub weapons are secondary munitions that require ink to dispense; they usually come in the form of defensive structures or offensive projectiles. Special weapons are powerful armaments that must be individually charged by inking the surroundings. Cosmetic gear can be augmented with abilities such as being able to swim faster within their ink and increasing ink ammunition capacity.

cards.heading: Turf War
cards.text: Splatoon 2 sees the return of Turf War and Ranked Battles from its predecessor. The game adds League Battles as a tournament-structured version of Ranked Battles. In Turf War, players are divided into two teams of four as they compete to spread more of their colored ink across a battle arena after three minutes.

cards.heading: Salmon Run
cards.text: Salmon Run is a co-op player versus environment mode first introduced in Splatoon 2. Salmon Run is available only on certain days at Grizzco. Players are placed into a team of four and tasked to defeat hordes of hostile salmon enemies, named Salmonids, and deposit Golden Eggs to meet a designated quota for a particular "wave", of which there are three total. Golden Eggs are acquired by splatting large Boss Salmonid enemies that each have distinct attack patterns and weaknesses. Successfully completing matches advances the player's rank in Grizzco, with the mode's difficulty increasing in tandem. Being splatted by a Salmonid results in the player being incapacitated until a teammate manually revives them. The match ends prematurely if all four team members are splatted at once.

cards.heading: Octo Canyon
cards.text: The game features a single-player campaign called Octo Canyon, in which the player rescues captured Zapfish across various levels while fighting off evil Octarians. Unlike the previous game's single-player campaign which had a pre-determined weapon set, the player can now earn various weapons, some of which are required when playing levels for the first time. In addition to Sunken Scrolls that unlock artwork and in-game lore, players can collect Power Orbs to upgrade their Hero Mode weapons, and tickets that can be exchanged for temporary reward boosts in multiplayer battles, such as increased experience to level up quicker or more in-game currency. Using a single weapon to beat all of the Hero Mode levels grants the player a Hero Weapon Replica (identical to the campaign weapon) to use in multiplayer matches.
